description.narrative: (State Western Hemisphere Regional): .Quality crime data and analysis is outdated in most Caribbean countries, limiting resources for effective decision-making on a comprehensive approach to youth crime and violence prevention. If Caribbean national authorities have access to standardized and disaggregated crime data reporting, it will improve the enabling environment for effective youth crime and violence prevention with reliable and comparable data for citizen security policy and decision making. Building on milestones achieved under the activity thus far, USAID will continue to support improved data-driven decision-making by strengthening the capacity of criminal justice agencies to better collect, analyze, and target crime administrative data. This support includes national survey data to inform policies that aim to address the root causes of crime and violence. Additionally, USAID will support the procurement and establishment of crime information management systems to equip law enforcement with the tools to accomplish these goals. These efforts will align crime and violence reporting indicators in the region to international standards, pilot a digitized police crime incident reporting system that transitions police from a paper-based to digitized recording crime system; and produce national surveys on gender-based violence and crime victimization... .
